column1: When I have a problem to solve, I find out as much information as I can about it.
column2: I try to think of many different approaches when I’m solving a problem.
column3: When I make a decision, I go with my "gut feeling" and I don’t think too much about the consequences.
column4: I spend a lot of time thinking about how what I do today will affect me in the future.
column5: I’d rather save my money for an important purchase than spend it immediately on something that doesn’t matter much to me.
column6: I will give up what I want today to get what I want in the future.
column7: I finish my homework on or before the due date.
column8: It’s easy for me to stop myself from buying things I can’t afford.
column9: When my family buys me things, I try to “pay them back" by helping them out.
column10: I feel personal responsibility when spending my family’s money.
column11: I don’t care if other people have more money than I do.
column12: I think it’s important to save money for things I want to buy or have.
column13: I think it’s important to save money for my education and my future.
column14: When I’m feeling down, I buy things to cheer myself up.
column15: I keep track of how much money I spend.
column16: Before I buy something, I ask myself if I need it or just want it.
column17: If I really want something, I work hard to get it.
column18: I let my friends’ choices guide what I decide to buy.
column19: I’m confident in my ability to achieve a financial goal I set.
column20: When I’m in trouble or have a challenge to deal with, I can usually find a solution.
column21: I’m good at making money decisions and managing money.
column22: How much a person charges on their credit card will affect their credit rating.
column23: A good rule to live by is to have an emergency fund that covers two to six months of expenses.
column24: Compound interest lets me earn interest on my principal and my interest.
column25: Because of compound interest, the earlier I start saving for retirement, the more money I’ll have when I retire.
column26: If a person uses their home as a guarantee for a loan, they could lose their home.
column27: If a person has an adjustable-rate mortgage and the interest rate goes up, their monthly mortgage payments will go up.
column28: I only trust information I find on the Internet if I know it’s from a reliable, factual source.
column29: To decide if I can trust what I read, I think about its purpose (for example, is it selling something?).
column30: Researching products and comparison shopping can help me make buying decisions that are best for me.
